go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ esutil.BulkIndexer with auto-batching, configurable size limits, per-item callbacks, retry logic
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ opensearchutil.BulkIndexer with FlushBytes (default 5MB), FlushInterval (30s), per-item callbacks, stats tracking
notes: Both support bulk indexing with size control (fixes #2192 bug). go-elasticsearch BulkIndexer: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esutil#BulkIndexer; opensearch-go BulkIndexer: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/v4/opensearchutil#BulkIndexer

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Configurable via BulkIndexer options; forward compatible handling of size thresholds
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ FlushBytes parameter (default 5MB) controls batch size; prevents exceeding request limits
notes: Critical for AWS OpenSearch 10MB HTTP limit. Both clients implement proper size-based flushing (unlike olivere/elastic where BulkSize was misinterpreted)

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ typedapi provides type-safe query builders; esapi for low-level JSON queries
opensearch-go_v4: ⚠️ opensearchapi low-level only; requires manual JSON construction or external DSL library
notes: go-elasticsearch has richer query building with typedapi. Source: https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/client/go-api/current/typedapi.html vs https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/clients/go/

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Full support via Search() in both typedapi and esapi
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Full support via opensearchapi.SearchReq
notes: Both support standard search operations. Examples in respective docs

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Supported via Scroll() methods in esapi and typedapi
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Supported via opensearchapi (confirmed in package docs)
notes: Both support scroll for large result sets. go-elasticsearch: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esapi#ScrollRequest

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Supported in ES 7.10+ via OpenPointInTime/ClosePointInTime APIs
opensearch-go_v4: ⚠️ Not explicitly documented; may require manual API calls
notes: PIT introduced in ES 7.10; OpenSearch forked from ES 7.10.2. go-elasticsearch docs: https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/point-in-time-api.html

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ DeleteByQuery() in esapi and typedapi packages
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ DeleteByQuery supported via opensearchapi
notes: Both support delete-by-query. go-elasticsearch: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esapi#DeleteByQueryRequest

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Full lifecycle: Create, Delete, GetSettings, PutSettings, PutMapping, Clone, Shrink, Split
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Create, Delete, GetSettings, PutSettings, PutMapping (advanced ops not explicitly documented)
notes: go-elasticsearch has more comprehensive index management APIs. Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esapi#pkg-index

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Rollover() via esapi and typedapi with conditions support
opensearch-go_v4: ⚠️ Rollover likely supported but not prominently documented
notes: Jaeger uses rollover for time-based index management. go-elasticsearch: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esapi#IndicesRolloverRequest

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ GetAlias, PutAlias, DeleteAlias, UpdateAliases (atomic multi-operation)
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Alias operations supported via opensearchapi
notes: Both support alias management for index abstraction. go-elasticsearch: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esapi#IndicesGetAliasRequest

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ PutTemplate, GetTemplate, DeleteTemplate, PutIndexTemplate (composable templates in ES 7.8+)
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Template operations supported (confirmed in docs examples)
notes: Jaeger uses templates for span/dependency indices. go-elasticsearch: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v9/esapi#IndicesPutTemplateRequest

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ ILM APIs in esapi: PutLifecycle, GetLifecycle, ExplainLifecycle, etc
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ ISM (Index State Management) plugin available in opensearch-go/v4/plugins/ism
notes: ES uses ILM; OpenSearch uses ISM (similar but different). opensearch-go ISM: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/v4/plugins/ism

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ ClusterHealth() with wait_for_status, timeout options
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ ClusterHealth supported via opensearchapi
notes: Both support cluster health checks for initialization/monitoring

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Search() accepts multiple indices via index parameter (comma-separated or array)
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Search() with multiple indices supported
notes: Jaeger queries across date-sharded indices (jaeger-span-*)

go-elasticsearch_v9: ⚠️ Requires external AWS SDK v2 sigv4 integration
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Built-in signer package (awsv2) for seamless AWS OpenSearch authentication
notes: opensearch-go has native AWS support which is critical for issue #2192 AWS deployments. Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/v4/signer/awsv2

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Configurable via transport.Config; supports custom headers, TLS, retry logic
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Configurable via opensearch.Config; similar transport customization
notes: Both allow low-level HTTP customization for enterprise requirements

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Multiple error types (ResponseError, etc) with structured access to status codes and body
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Multiple error types (StringError, StructError, ReasonError, MessageError) for different ES/OS response formats
notes: opensearch-go has more granular error types. Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/v4#pkg-types

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ OpenTelemetry instrumentation support via config
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Metrics collection via config.EnableMetrics; custom logger interfaces (TextLogger, ColorLogger, CurlLogger, JSONLogger)
notes: opensearch-go has richer built-in logging options. Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/v4#Config

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Automatic via default transport; configurable max connections
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ Automatic via opensearchtransport; node discovery with configurable intervals
notes: Both handle connection pooling; opensearch-go has explicit node discovery intervals

go-elasticsearch_v9: ✅ Forward compatible with ES 7.x, 8.x, 9.x (communicates with >= minor versions); separate v7, v8, v9 modules available
opensearch-go_v4: ✅ OpenSearch 1.3.20 - 3.0.0; breaking changes between major versions
notes: go-elasticsearch more permissive (forward compatible); opensearch-go stricter version alignment. Sources: https://github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch README, https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/blob/main/COMPATIBILITY.md
